newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada spot gas prices surge amid cold weather.
newsitem.headline: Canada spot gas prices surge amid cold weather.

text.p: Canadian spot natural gas prices for October surged across the board on Wednesday as snow and cold weather blanketed western Canada and producers entered the market to purchase supply, marketing sources said.
Spot gas at the AECO storage hub in Alberta was talked in the C$1.29/1.30 range, up from C$1.19/1.195 last week. November gas was quoted at C$1.29/1.305 per GJ.

The high demand meant a net storage withdrawal in Alberta of just over 40 million cubic feet per day, traders said. "(Prices) might come off slightly from here," said a marketer, who added temperatures were forecast to rise later this week.
"But that's what I've said for quite a while now. It's why producers, I think, are buying -- on the expection that prices would have been soft," the marketer said.
At the borders, prices for gas destined for the U.S. Midwest and Pacific Northwest were also much stronger than last week's levels.

Gas at Monchy, Saskatchewan was talked up about a dime on the week to US$1.47 per million British thermal units, as below-normal temperatures moved into the central United States. Gas at the British Columbia-Washington border was quoted at in the upper US$1.20s, but was also projected by traders to decrease later this week.
